title: Crianza Positiva: Combining Group Workshops and E-Messages to Strengthen Parenting Competences
metadata.scope: Bibliographic identity only; different DOI/title/year alone does not prove a distinct original finding.

sample_dates_centers_groups.statement: 41 centers signed up;24 received training,17 deferred. Workshop access was first come, not randomized. Both intervention and comparison families already attended weekly unstructured CAIF playgroups.

After workshops, the24 implementing centers were randomized by maternal-education strata:14 to messaging and10 to no messaging. Manuscript describes three arms with initial N759: workshop+messages237, workshop only292, no workshop/no messages230.

Observed analysis contains442 dyads:126 workshop+messages,193 workshop only,123 unstructured-playgroup controls;58% recorded at follow-up. Mean child age19 months at workshop initiation. Exact calendar implementation dates are not stated in the inspected recruitment passage; timing relative to workshop/message completion is explicit. Calendar2017–2018 linkage is supported by companion-report comparisons, not inferred from publication year.
Follow-up was more than9 months after workshop and1–3 months after messaging; program had8 group sessions and6-month messaging.

measurements_and_findings.statement: Main outcomes are observed free-play child-caregiver interaction quality rated with PICCOLO, not an E2P self-report competence score. Domains: affection, responsiveness, teaching. Encouragement excluded for poor inter-rater reliability. Professional coders were blind to treatment; main IPW cross-section comparison addresses nonrandom workshop allocation.

Table3: workshop only vs untreated PICCOLO total+3.471,SE1.088,d0.46,p<.01; workshop+messages vs untreated+3.850,SE0.849,d0.53,p<.01. Direct message increment vs workshop only total+0.947,SE0.709,d0.13,no significance star.

Table3 workshop only vs untreated: affection+1.197,SE.374,d.44,p<.01; responsiveness+.703,SE.383,d.24,p<.10; teaching+1.570,SE.549,d.44,p<.01. Workshop+messages vs untreated: affection+1.601,SE.352,d.59,p<.01; responsiveness+1.028,SE.427,d.37,p<.05; teaching+1.221,SE.466,d.37,p<.01.
Direct workshop+messages vs workshop only: affection+.531,SE.212,d.20,p<.05; responsiveness+.535,SE.244,d.20,p<.05; teaching−.118,SE.409,d−.03,not significant.

This is a factual report comparison only. No empirical-target equivalence or coding verdict is assigned.

title: Effect of Crianza Positiva e-messaging program on adult–child language interactions
metadata.scope: Bibliographic identity only; different DOI/title/year alone does not prove a distinct original finding.

sample_dates_centers_groups.statement: 24CAIF centers after8-week workshop; December2017 two-stage randomized assignment. Initial529 families:237 messages,59 no messages within14 treated centers,233 pure controls in10 control centers. AEARCTR-0003585.
Messages January5–June27,2018; controls one thank-you SMS January26. Baselines August2017 and November–December2017; follow-up August–November2018.

317 follow-up videos (122 treated,195 controls);178 dyads with baseline and follow-up videos (80 treated,98 controls). Core regressions have157–159 observations depending on endpoint/covariate availability; core pitch range N158. These regression Ns differ from collection Ns.

measurements_and_findings.statement: Automated analysis of audio extracted from10-minute video-recorded free play. Counts and durations of child/adult vocalizations, total duration, conversational turns, adult response ratio, adult mean pitch and pitch range. These are acoustic interaction endpoints, not standardized child language-test scores.

Core Table3 adult pitch range ITT+.424 ERB,SE.147,approximately18% above control2.42; unadjusted p<.01,wild-bootstrap p=.066,Romano–Wolf multiplicity p=.016. Spillover pitch+.405,SE.235,unadjusted p<.10,WB=.077,MHT=.308.

Core duration child−44.668 seconds,SE22.819; adult+28.993,SE17.265; both unadjusted p<.10. Adult WB p=.289; child WB=.095; MHT p=.269 adult,.193 child. Authors call duration changes nonrobust. Narrative says “seconds per vocalization” but Table3 labels total duration in seconds; no unit repair is made silently.

No statistically significant effects on adult/child vocalization counts,total vocalization duration,conversational turns,adult responsiveness or average pitch in core Table3. Broader follow-up-only sample pitch and child-duration effects lose significance with center clustering; core pitch result is not generalized to every specification.

Survey mechanisms: standardized reading+.295,telling stories+.271,naming/telling/drawing+.437,aggregate literacy involvement+.374; respective WB p=.077,.047,.007,.012. Singing outcomes not significant. Self-reports are separate from the acoustic endpoints.

sample_dates_centers_groups.statement: Workshops September–November2017 in24CAIF centers; messages January5–June27,2018. Two-stage RCT:529families,14treated centers296families,10pure-control centers233families; within treated centers237messages and59spillover controls. Entire no-message group292.

171 of237treated families responded at follow-up (72%); controls78%,Table3 response rate.777. Outcome-specific missingness changes Ns. Survey follow-up August–November2018. Control families got a single thank-you SMS January26.

measurements_and_findings.statement: Self-administered caregiver questionnaire in interviewer presence: quantity/quality of parental investment,knowledge,self-efficacy,stress,time preferences. Quantity includes Cabrera-derived physical/social/caring/didactic activity frequencies,Etxadi-Gangoiti father involvement and material resources/books/toys.

Quality uses a subset of E2P positive-parenting items (not full scale),with attachment,routines,social-support,reflection subindices; discipline from UNICEF MICS6. PSOC effectiveness/controllability assess perceived competence,distinct from E2P behavior and observed PICCOLO. PSI/SF covers parental discomfort,dysfunctional interaction,difficult child. MCQ measures time preference;13true/false knowledge items.

Main covariate-adjusted Table6 column3 time-investment index+.330SD,SE.122; clustering p=.006,MHT=.010,randomization inference=.011. Physical games+.273SD,SE.117;didactic+.292,SE.106;social+.269,SE.121. Baseline-adjusted column4 index+.300,physical+.295,didactic+.254,social+.193.

Table6 column3 E2P subset index+.309SD,SE.124;cluster p=.003,MHT=.040,RI=.003. Social support+.251SD,SE.108,MHT=.089;reflection+.334,SE.116,MHT=.020. Attachment+.104 and routines+.101 not significant. No significant main effects on violent discipline,father involvement,books.

No evidence of main effects on parental stress,discount rate or parenting knowledge. PSOC effectiveness positive with unadjusted p-values but nonsignificant after clustering/MHT;controllability nonsignificant. Thus “parental competence improved” cannot stand in for every competence measure.
